verses.english: Linked Discourses 56.31
4. In a Rosewood Forest
In a Rosewood Forest

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati sīsapāvane.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in a rosewood grove.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā parittāni sīsapāpaṇṇāni pāṇinā gahetvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha picked up a few rosewood leaves in his hand and addressed the mendicants:
“What do you think, mendicants?
Which is more:

verses.pali: yāni vā mayā parittāni sīsapāpaṇṇāni pāṇinā gahitāni yadidaṁ upari sīsapāvane”ti?
verses.english: the few leaves in my hand, or those in the grove above?”

verses.pali: “Appamattakāni, bhante, bhagavatā parittāni sīsapāpaṇṇāni pāṇinā gahitāni;
verses.english: “Sir, the few leaves in your hand are a tiny amount.

verses.pali: atha kho etāneva bahutarāni yadidaṁ upari sīsapāvane”ti.
verses.english: There are far more leaves in the grove above.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, etadeva bahutaraṁ yaṁ vo mayā abhiññāya anakkhātaṁ.
verses.english: “In the same way, there is much more that I have directly known but have not explained to you. What I have explained is a tiny amount.
And why haven’t I explained it?

verses.pali: Na hetaṁ, bhikkhave, atthasaṁhitaṁ nādibrahmacariyakaṁ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati;
verses.english: Because it’s not beneficial or relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.
That’s why I haven’t explained it.
And what have I explained?

verses.pali: ‘Idaṁ dukkhan’ti, bhikkhave, mayā akkhātaṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti mayā akkhātaṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti mayā akkhātaṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti mayā akkhātaṁ.
verses.english: I have explained: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
And why have I explained this?

verses.pali: Etañhi, bhikkhave, atthasaṁhitaṁ etaṁ ādibrahmacariyakaṁ etaṁ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati;
verses.english: Because it’s beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It leads to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.
That’s why I’ve explained it.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”
